notes: How this part was researched: the session's shared web-search allowance was already used up, so no search engine was read. Pages were opened directly with the kit's honest User-Agent (each site's robots.txt read first and obeyed) or with the page-reading tool: the campaign websites the candidates filed (already in sl_websites, read read-only), each county's, city's and school district's own site, the Minnesota DFL's list of endorsed candidates, the DFL Environmental Caucus, the Minnesota House and the Legislative Reference Library, and the Metropolitan Airports Commission.

nelsonfor21a.com answered the script with 429 (too many requests) on most tries; the home page was read once by the script and its About page with the page-reading tool. The second reader may meet the same 429.

Cedrick Frazier: the Minnesota DFL's endorsed list covers statewide, congressional and legislative seats only and does not name him; no party page with the county attorney endorsement was found (the Hennepin County DFL's address did not resolve), so the endorsement is recorded only as his own words. His campaign site also lists the Working Families Party; that party's own page was not looked for.

Amáda Márquez Simula: the City of Columbia Heights' robots.txt asks scripts to stay out, so the mayor's office rests on her campaign site. The DFL Environmental Caucus is a caucus of the party; its page is headed Endorsements and describes her; left for the second reader to judge whether it stands under endorsed_by.
Matt Bliss and John Hoffman are sitting legislators with record pages. No Republican party page naming Matt Bliss for 2026 was found (no local unit's address was known without a search).

The official pages read show these candidates do not hold the office sought today: Pipestone County lists Doug Nagel for District 2 (Thomas Haag) and Keith Vreeman as sheriff (Dustin Seiler); Norman County lists Steve Jacobson for District 3 (Angela Nelson); Anoka's mayor is Erik Skogquist (Phil Rice); Adam P. Woodruff, Emily Antin, Tim Hudacek, Brandy Maki, Tyler Hemmesch and Ryan Vernosh are not on the Little Canada, Richfield, Red Wing, Hibbing, St. Michael-Albertville and White Bear Lake pages read. Any earlier offices they may have held could not be looked up without a search.

Not reached, and nothing worked around: the Minnesota Judicial Branch (its robots.txt keeps scripts out), so nothing is recorded for Rachel C. Sullivan; Red Lake County's site (a certificate that does not match its name), so nothing for Allen Remick; the Sartell-St. Stephen and St. Louis County school districts' sites (no answer), so nothing for Chris Chamberlain or Kerie Porter; the Cloquet and Litchfield districts' board pages load their names by script and showed none, so nothing for Victoria M.L. McMillen or Gregory Dean Mathews. Benton County's sheriff page does not name James Dingmann; his campaign site describes employment in the sheriff's office, which is not an office held.

Privacy: while reading two government pages (Hibbing's council page and Norman County's board page) a few officials' published contact lines were printed to the working log before the filter was tightened. Nothing of the kind was stored or written here.

verifier_notes: Every url in the file was re-opened on 2026-10-02 with the kit's honest User-Agent; nelsonfor21a.com answered 429 twice and was read with the page-reading tool. Each filed website was also checked against sl_websites (read-only).

Same-person anchors: each campaign site names the candidate and the office or place sought; each official page names the person under the body our record shows (Winona County Fifth District; New Ulm mayor; Champlin Ward 4; Kasson-Mantorville board; the MAC page places Kyle O'Neill in Chanhassen; the House and Library pages are tied to the Hennepin County Attorney race by his campaign site's "a State Representative").

Cedrick Frazier's full birth date comes from an official page (the Legislative Reference Library), which the rules allow. The same record also prints birthplace, minority status, schooling and occupation: none of that is in this file and none should be taken from it.

The DFL Environmental Caucus endorsement was kept because it is on the caucus's own page under a 2026 heading and the caucus is part of the party; the unit says plainly that it is the caucus, not the party's convention. If John wants only convention endorsements shown, drop that one entry.
Both own_words quotes are on the candidates' own home pages and are within twelve words (twelve and eleven).
Candidates with no findings were left blank; the researcher's notes about who does not hold the office today record no fact about a person and were not re-checked.
